scenes.desc: Cantes alegres de la bahía de Cádiz, en compás de soleá y muy ligados al baile, que arranca majestuoso y va ganando fuerza hasta desplantes electrizantes. Nacen probablemente de la jotilla gaditana, hermanada con la jota aragonesa por la resistencia común contra Napoleón, de ahí las letras sobre la guerra y el mar; la leyenda atribuye su creación a Enrique el Mellizo, que oyó a una muchacha cantar jotas con un ciego. Tomaron identidad en la segunda mitad del XIX. Hay cantiñas del Pinini de Utrera y Lebrija y de Córdoba; la rosa ya no se canta. Las alegrías, al principio baile de mujer sola, se hicieron más lentas a comienzos del XX y empiezan con el «tirititrán» que, según Chano Lobato, inventó Pericón de Cádiz al olvidar la letra; las cantaron el Mellizo, Ignacio Ezpeleta, Aurelio Sellés, Manolo Vargas y Pericón. Los caracoles, de Tío José el Granaíno (picador del Chiclanero), los recreó Chacón y triunfaron en Madrid («la gran calle de Alcalá»). El mirabrás son alegrías largas (José Menese, con letras de Moreno Galván), y las romeras se atribuyen al Granaíno o a una cantaora llamada la Romera. Hoy el gran intérprete es Chano Lobato.

scenes.name: Los tangos, tientos y marianas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Con bulerías y cantiñas, el gran cante festero: letras de vida, amor y muerte con cierta ligereza, ritmo vivo y pegadizo fácil de seguir con palmas, y un baile sensual. Cádiz y Sevilla se disputan su paternidad, pero los hay en toda Andalucía y en Extremadura; Triana tiene el estilo del Titi y Jerez su propio sello. Su origen musical se discute: Mairena los tenía por cante básico gitano; los estudios recientes los llevan a Cuba y las habaneras llegadas a Sevilla y Cádiz en la segunda mitad del XIX; los granadinos defienden una raíz morisca (el disco Granada canta por tangos recoge trece estilos, entre ellos los de la morería). Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: New Generation's Chart Domination (1994)
facts.body: By 1994, a new generation of "pure punk" bands, influenced by the Ramones, such as Offspring, Rancid, and Green Day, "overtook the modern rock and even the pop charts." This explosion of punk came too late for the original bands like The Ramones. "A new generation of what you might call pure punk of the Ramones variety, led by bands like Offspring, Rancid and Green Day overtook the modern rock and even the pop charts by 1994."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: This Ain’t No Party! Edition Part 2
facts.name: Punk

facts.title: New Generation's Chart Domination (1994)

facts.title: Final Show March 1, 1994; Death April 8, 1994 – The Vacuum That Reshaped 1994's Rock Landscape
facts.body: Nirvana played their final concert in Munich on March 1, 1994 — Kurt's voice was shot, the band was exhausted, and the rest of the European tour was canceled. On March 3, he deliberately overdosed on tranquilizers in a Rome hotel room. On March 18, police were called to his Seattle house after he locked himself in a room with guns. He agreed to enter rehab after an intervention, then escaped. His body was found April 8. The news was read on air: "Nirvana lead singer Kurt Cobain shot himself to death at a Seattle home yesterday." The effect on music fans was profound and prolonged. The loss of Nirvana's central narrative created a temporary opening that Green Day, The Offspring, Blur, and Oasis each rushed to fill. "Kurt's death was extremely traumatic. And the mourning continued for months."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Final Concert (Munich, March 1, 1994) – Preserved Only by Bootleg Recording
facts.body: The last live performance by Kurt Cobain with Nirvana, on March 1, 1994, in Munich, was preserved for posterity exclusively through a bootleg recording. Had that recording not been made, the concert would have been entirely lost to history. "The last live performance of Kurt Cobain with Nirvana on March 1, 1994 in Munich was preserved exclusively by a bootleg recording."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: The discovery of Kurt Cobain's death occurred on April 8, 1994, just two months after Green Day's Dookie was released. This tragic event profoundly influenced the musical landscape, causing the "heaviness and bleakness of Grunge" to seem "a little too much" for audiences, thereby paving the way for the emergence of the lighter pop punk sound. "Two months after Duckey was released, Kurt Cobain was found dead."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Last Concert (Munich, March 1994)
facts.body: Nirvana's final performance was in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, in March 1994, for just over 3,000 people. The show included a quick acoustic set due to a power failure and a cover of The Cars' "My Best Friend's Girl." "Nirvana's last ever show was held in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany. In March of 1994, in front of just over 3,000 people."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: End of Band (1994)
facts.body: Nirvana concluded its run in 1994. Following this, Dave Grohl started the Foo Fighters in 1995, retaining John Silva as his manager through this transition and all subsequent developments.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Intervention and Second Rehab Stint (1994)
facts.body: On March 25th, 1994, an intervention by friends, family, and business associates convinced Kurt Cobain to address his self-destructive behavior and heroin addiction. He reluctantly agreed to try rehab again, checking into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles on Thursday, March 30th. "On March 25th, 1994, an intervention of friends, family, and business associates convinced Kurt that his self-destructive tendencies brought on by his heroin issues had to stop, so he reluctantly and angrily agreed to try rehab again."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Rehab Escape (1994)
facts.body: While at the Exodus Recovery Center, Kurt Cobain befriended fellow patient Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers. On the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, 1994, at 7:25 PM, Cobain told an attendant he was going for a smoke, then scaled a six-foot fence to escape, despite being able to simply walk out under Exodus policy. "Instead, he scaled the six-foot fence and made a break for it, which was unnecessarily dramatic, since under Exodus policy, he could have just walked out the front door."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan and Death (1994)
facts.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took Delta Flight 788 to Seattle and coincidentally sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan, also a veteran of rehab. Cobain refused a ride from McKagan upon landing, signed autographs, and disappeared. He then acquired drugs, returned to the room above the greenhouse at his and Courtney Love's Lake Washington Boulevard home, got high, and died by suicide, believed to be on April 5th, 1994. The news of his death broke on Friday, April 8th. "Soon, he was on Delta Flight 788 to Seattle, and by sheer coincidence, he was sitting next to Guns & Roses bass player Duff McAgan, himself, a junkie we have veteran."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: On Friday, April 8, 1994, Kurt Cobain's body was discovered in his Seattle home. Police reported that a man in his 20s was found with a shotgun wound to the head, and a suicide note was nearby. An electrician doing work at the home found the body through a window, leading police to break into a cottage above a detached garage where the discovery was made. Cobain had been recuperating from an overdose of painkillers and champagne the previous month in Rome. His mother mentioned he had been missing for six days and that she had advised him not to join the "stupid club of other rock stars who had died early." Initially reported as 28, Cobain was 27 at the time of his death. "The record company official says Nirvana leads singer Kurt Cobain shot himself to death at his Seattle home yesterday."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 1000th Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Lead Singer Kurt Cobain's Death (April 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain died in April 1994, a tragic event that created a significant void and brought hurt and confusion to the Grunge and Grunge-Lite communities, prompting a reluctant shift in the music scene to find "the next, next big thing." "And then in April 1994, Kurt died, and that brought nothing but hurt and confusion to the whole Grunge and Grunge-Lite community."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Peak of Fourth Cycle (Pre-1994)
facts.body: The peak of rock's fourth cycle came shortly before Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994, indicating that the genre's momentum began to decline around that time. "The peak for this cycle came shortly before Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Intervention for Kurt Cobain (March 25, 1994)
facts.body: Nirvana bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, along with touring guitarist Pat Smear, participated in a five-hour intervention for Kurt Cobain at his Seattle home. This was an attempt by his wife Courtney Love and others to convince him to address his drug problems, following a previous suicide attempt in Rome. "This group included Courtney, his bandmates, Chris Nova's Selaj and Dave Grohl, touring Nirvana guitars, Pat Smir, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Last Live Show (March 1994)
facts.body: Nirvana's final performance took place on March 1, 1994, in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, before an audience of approximately 3,000 people. Kurt Cobain was unwell, suffering from a sore throat, and the performance was not up to par, leading to the cancellation of the remainder of the tour so he could recover from chronic bronchitis and laryngitis. "Nirvana's last ever show was staged in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany on March 1, 1994, in front of about 3,000 people."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Rome Suicide Attempt (March 1994)
facts.body: While on a supposed vacation in Rome with Courtney Love, Kurt Cobain made a suicide attempt by ingesting around 50 Rohypnol pills with champagne, which caused him to slip into a coma. Although he recovered in the hospital, some news networks erroneously reported his death. "He downed about 50 Rohipnopils with some champagne and slipped into a coma. He recovered in hospital, but not before some networks reported that he died."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Shotgun Purchase Through a Friend (March 1994)
facts.body: On March 30, 1994, Kurt Cobain went with his friend Dylan Carlson to Stan Baker's Sports and purchased a shotgun for $303.37. The purchase was officially made by Dylan because the police had previously confiscated all of Cobain's numerous other firearms, viewing him as a threat to himself. "On March 30, he and his friend Dylan Carlson went together to stand Baker's sports where he bought a shotgun for $303.37."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Escape from Rehab (April 1994)
facts.body: After reluctantly agreeing to an intervention by friends and bandmates, Kurt Cobain checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles. However, he stayed for only two nights before slipping out on the evening of April 1, taking a cab to the airport. "He stayed two nights but then slipped out on the evening of April 1."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Suicide (April 1994)
facts.body: Sometime on Tuesday, April 5, Kurt Cobain went to the room above the greenhouse in his backyard. There, he wrote a suicide note expressing his anguish and apologizing for his actions, including lines from a Neil Young song, "it's better to burn out than fade away." He then loaded the shotgun, gave himself a massive injection of heroin, put away his drug paraphernalia, and shot himself in the head. His body was discovered by an electrician on the morning of Friday, April 8, 1994. "He wrote a suicide note, detailing his anguish, apologizing for what he was about to do. The note included some lines from a Neil Young song. It's better to burn out than fade away. Kurt then loaded the shotgun and gave himself a massive injection of heroin. After putting all his drug paraphernalia away, he turned the gunner himself and shot himself in the head."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Last Concert (March 1, 1994) – Terminal 1, Munich
facts.body: Nirvana played their final show as a band on March 1, 1994, at Terminal 1 in Munich during a European tour. At the time, Kurt Cobain was suffering from bronchitis. The show, held in a former airport terminal, opened with a cover of The Cars' "My Best Friend's Girl," experienced a power outage during "Come As You Are," and notably omitted "Smells Like Teen Spirit." The band performed a 23-song setlist, with "Heart-Shaped Box" being their last live song. "The last show Nirvana ever played. I'll give you the date, March 1, 1994. Nirvana was in the midst of a European tour, and Kurt was not doing well."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Lasts
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: European Tour Cancellation (March 1994)
facts.body: Following their performance at Terminal 1 in Munich on March 1, 1994, the remainder of Nirvana's European tour was cancelled. This decision was made because Kurt Cobain was deemed unfit to continue, suffering from bronchitis and a sore throat. The other band members, Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl, also needed a vacation, with Novoselic returning to Seattle and Grohl remaining in Germany to work on a film soundtrack. "After that show, the rest of the European tour was cancelled."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Dylan Carlson Friendship and Shotgun Purchase (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain maintained a close friendship with Dylan Carlson. On March 30, 1994, Carlson accompanied Cobain to Stan Baker's Sports in Seattle, where they purchased a Remington M11 shotgun for $308.37. Accounts differ on whether Kurt directly paid for it or if Dylan made the actual purchase after receiving money from Kurt. "He was Kurt's best friend, and he was the guy who went with Kurt to Stan Baker's Sports in Seattle, on March 30, 1994, to buy a Remington M11 shotgun for $308.37. Actually, some stories say that Kurt gave him the money, and Dylan was the person who actually bought it."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Rome Overdose Incident (March 4, 1994)
facts.body: While in Rome, taking medication, Kurt Cobain was found on the morning of March 4, 1994, in his hotel room with Kurt Ylov, having suffered a massive overdose and fallen into a coma. The overdose was reportedly caused by sedatives and champagne. "la mañana siguiente, el 4 de marzo de 1994, Kurt Cobain aparece en la habitación de su tal con Kurt Ylov como una enorme sobredosis y en coma."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Seattle Police Call (March 18, 1994)
facts.body: On March 18, Kurt Ylov called the police to their Seattle home, claiming Kurt Cobain had locked himself in a room with a weapon and intended to commit suicide. Police found Kurt locked in a room but he had no weapon and no suicidal intent, stating he was merely tired of arguing with Kurt Ylov. "el 18 de marzo está en siete en su casa, Kurt Ylov llama la policía."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Drug Intervention (March 25, 1994)
facts.body: On March 25, Kurt Ylov organized a drug intervention for Kurt Cobain, attended by Nirvana band members, Geffen record label executives, and two of his best friends, to address his heroin problem. Kurt Cobain was very negative about the process, and initially denied having a major addiction, instead claiming Kurt Ylov was the one with the problem. "el 25 de marzo, o cosas más tarde, Kurt Ylov decía hace una especie de intervención de las drogas para Kurt Cobain."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Admission to Los Angeles Detox Center (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain officially entered the Los Angeles detox center on March 30, 1994. Reports from the center were positive, indicating he was doing well, his health was improving, he had a positive attitude, played guitar often, and received visitors. "El 30 de marzo, unos días después, ingresa oficialmente en el centro de los áncieles de desintoxicación."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Visit from Daughter and Nanny (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On April 1, Kurt Cobain received a visit from his young daughter and her nanny at the detox center. He was happy with his daughter, and the nanny noted a significant improvement in his condition. "el 1 de abril, él recibe una visita de su hija pequeña con la niñera que tenía."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Aggressive Call and Rehab Escape (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On the night of April 1, conflicting reports suggest Kurt Cobain received a very aggressive phone call from Kurt Ylov at the detox center, which may have contributed to his escape. Regardless, he escaped the center, took a plane, and flew to Seattle. "hay quien dice que esa misma noche recibe una llamada muy agresiva del cornylofa al centro de sintoxicación. Se a lo que fuese ese día, Curco Vence escapa del centro de sintoxicación, se cojo un avión y se va a hacerte."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Discovery of Kurt Cobain's Body (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: On April 8, 1994, an electrician installing a security device found Kurt Cobain dead on the floor of his home, which he shared with Kurt Ylov. Initially disbelieving he was dead, the electrician found a suicide note, then called the police who certified his death. "el 8 de abril de 1994 cuando un electricista entra en casa de Córkovend y de Córnilof y se encuentra Córkovend en el suelo muerto."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Official Date of Death (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: The autopsy revealed Kurt Cobain died on April 5, 1994. This date is significant as it was two days after Kurt Ylov hired a private detective to find him and the day before she reported to the police that he intended to die by gunshot. "la torce revela que Córkovend murió el 5 de abril."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Suicide as Pivot Point (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's tragic suicide in the spring of 1994 served as a sad but key pivot point in the evolution of alternative rock. Following this event, radio programmers and fans increasingly gravitated towards perkier, less dour music, contributing to the rise of bands like Hootie & the Blowfish and a general softening of the mainstream rock sound. "Especially after Kurt Cobain's tragic suicide in the spring of 1994. A sad but key pivot point in the evolution of all-truck, radio programmers and fans were increasingly turning toward this perky less-dour music."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: A Little Love and Some Tenderness Edition Part 1
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Biggest Band in America (1994)
facts.body: Going into 1994, Nirvana, alongside Pearl Jam, was regarded as one of the "unquestioned biggest bands in America," reflecting their immense influence and popularity. "Going into 1994, Nirvana and Pearl Jam were the unquestioned biggest bands in America."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: The discovery of Kurt Cobain's death occurred on April 8, 1994, just two months after Green Day's Dookie was released. This tragic event profoundly influenced the musical landscape, causing the "heaviness and bleakness of Grunge" to seem "a little too much" for audiences, thereby paving the way for the emergence of the lighter pop punk sound. "Two months after Duckey was released, Kurt Cobain was found dead."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: The short answer to whether Kurt Cobain was murdered is "no." However, many conspiracy theories persist, citing "unanswered questions" such as how he could inject a massive heroin overdose, put his gear away, and shoot himself before being incapacitated, the alleged change in handwriting on his suicide note, who used his credit card post-mortem, and why a room above the garden house wasn't checked during searches. These questions have fueled documentaries, books, and websites. Applying Occam's Razor, the "simplest answer is usually the correct one." Kurt was described as a depressed, unhealthy, hardcore heroin addict who associated with "very weird and bad people," had an obsession with guns, and was "certifiably suicidal." His body was so accustomed to heroin that a fatal dose might have had a delayed effect, allowing him time to put away a syringe and aim the gun. The murder theory is deemed "just chasing shadows," though the possibility of being wrong is acknowledged. "My short answer to this is no. Now there are all sorts of unanswered questions. How did Kurt manage to inject himself with a massive overdose of heroin, put his gear away in the maneuver the shot got in time before the drugs knocked him out? What about the fact that the handwriting on the suicide note appears to change? Who was using Kurt's credit card in the hours and days after he died? Why didn't anyone think to check the room above the garden house when they were searching for him?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: Hugh Dillon referenced Kurt Cobain's death as part of the perceived decline and bleakness in the music world that contributed to his anger and angst during his struggles with addiction. "Kurt Cobain's dead."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 2
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Final Concert (Munich, March 1, 1994) – Preserved Only by Bootleg Recording
facts.body: The last live performance by Kurt Cobain with Nirvana, on March 1, 1994, in Munich, was preserved for posterity exclusively through a bootleg recording. Had that recording not been made, the concert would have been entirely lost to history. "The last live performance of Kurt Cobain with Nirvana on March 1, 1994 in Munich was preserved exclusively by a bootleg recording."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Last Concert (March 1, 1994) – Terminal 1, Munich
facts.body: Nirvana played their final show as a band on March 1, 1994, at Terminal 1 in Munich during a European tour. At the time, Kurt Cobain was suffering from bronchitis. The show, held in a former airport terminal, opened with a cover of The Cars' "My Best Friend's Girl," experienced a power outage during "Come As You Are," and notably omitted "Smells Like Teen Spirit." The band performed a 23-song setlist, with "Heart-Shaped Box" being their last live song. "The last show Nirvana ever played. I'll give you the date, March 1, 1994. Nirvana was in the midst of a European tour, and Kurt was not doing well."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Lasts
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Last Concert (March 1, 1994) – Terminal 1, Munich
facts.body: Nirvana's final performance was in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, in March 1994, for just over 3,000 people. The show included a quick acoustic set due to a power failure and a cover of The Cars' "My Best Friend's Girl." "Nirvana's last ever show was held in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany. In March of 1994, in front of just over 3,000 people."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Last Concert (March 1, 1994) – Terminal 1, Munich
facts.body: Nirvana's final performance took place on March 1, 1994, in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, before an audience of approximately 3,000 people. Kurt Cobain was unwell, suffering from a sore throat, and the performance was not up to par, leading to the cancellation of the remainder of the tour so he could recover from chronic bronchitis and laryngitis. "Nirvana's last ever show was staged in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany on March 1, 1994, in front of about 3,000 people."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain died in April 1994, a tragic event that created a significant void and brought hurt and confusion to the Grunge and Grunge-Lite communities, prompting a reluctant shift in the music scene to find "the next, next big thing." "And then in April 1994, Kurt died, and that brought nothing but hurt and confusion to the whole Grunge and Grunge-Lite community."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Official Date of Death (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: The autopsy revealed Kurt Cobain died on April 5, 1994. This date is significant as it was two days after Kurt Ylov hired a private detective to find him and the day before she reported to the police that he intended to die by gunshot. "la torce revela que Córkovend murió el 5 de abril."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Peak of Fourth Cycle (Pre-1994)
facts.body: The peak of rock's fourth cycle came shortly before Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994, indicating that the genre's momentum began to decline around that time. "The peak for this cycle came shortly before Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Escape from Rehab (April 1994)
facts.body: While at the Exodus Recovery Center, Kurt Cobain befriended fellow patient Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers. On the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, 1994, at 7:25 PM, Cobain told an attendant he was going for a smoke, then scaled a six-foot fence to escape, despite being able to simply walk out under Exodus policy. "Instead, he scaled the six-foot fence and made a break for it, which was unnecessarily dramatic, since under Exodus policy, he could have just walked out the front door."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Rome Overdose Incident (March 4, 1994)
facts.body: While in Rome, taking medication, Kurt Cobain was found on the morning of March 4, 1994, in his hotel room with Kurt Ylov, having suffered a massive overdose and fallen into a coma. The overdose was reportedly caused by sedatives and champagne. "la mañana siguiente, el 4 de marzo de 1994, Kurt Cobain aparece en la habitación de su tal con Kurt Ylov como una enorme sobredosis y en coma."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Rome Suicide Attempt (March 1994)
facts.body: While on a supposed vacation in Rome with Courtney Love, Kurt Cobain made a suicide attempt by ingesting around 50 Rohypnol pills with champagne, which caused him to slip into a coma. Although he recovered in the hospital, some news networks erroneously reported his death. "He downed about 50 Rohipnopils with some champagne and slipped into a coma. He recovered in hospital, but not before some networks reported that he died."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Seattle Police Call (March 18, 1994)
facts.body: On March 18, Kurt Ylov called the police to their Seattle home, claiming Kurt Cobain had locked himself in a room with a weapon and intended to commit suicide. Police found Kurt locked in a room but he had no weapon and no suicidal intent, stating he was merely tired of arguing with Kurt Ylov. "el 18 de marzo está en siete en su casa, Kurt Ylov llama la policía."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Shotgun Purchase Through a Friend (March 1994)
facts.body: On March 30, 1994, Kurt Cobain went with his friend Dylan Carlson to Stan Baker's Sports and purchased a shotgun for $303.37. The purchase was officially made by Dylan because the police had previously confiscated all of Cobain's numerous other firearms, viewing him as a threat to himself. "On March 30, he and his friend Dylan Carlson went together to stand Baker's sports where he bought a shotgun for $303.37."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Suicide (April 1994)
facts.body: Sometime on Tuesday, April 5, Kurt Cobain went to the room above the greenhouse in his backyard. There, he wrote a suicide note expressing his anguish and apologizing for his actions, including lines from a Neil Young song, "it's better to burn out than fade away." He then loaded the shotgun, gave himself a massive injection of heroin, put away his drug paraphernalia, and shot himself in the head. His body was discovered by an electrician on the morning of Friday, April 8, 1994. "He wrote a suicide note, detailing his anguish, apologizing for what he was about to do. The note included some lines from a Neil Young song. It's better to burn out than fade away. Kurt then loaded the shotgun and gave himself a massive injection of heroin. After putting all his drug paraphernalia away, he turned the gunner himself and shot himself in the head."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Visit from Daughter and Nanny (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On April 1, Kurt Cobain received a visit from his young daughter and her nanny at the detox center. He was happy with his daughter, and the nanny noted a significant improvement in his condition. "el 1 de abril, él recibe una visita de su hija pequeña con la niñera que tenía."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Suicide as Pivot Point (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's tragic suicide in the spring of 1994 served as a sad but key pivot point in the evolution of alternative rock. Following this event, radio programmers and fans increasingly gravitated towards perkier, less dour music, contributing to the rise of bands like Hootie & the Blowfish and a general softening of the mainstream rock sound. "Especially after Kurt Cobain's tragic suicide in the spring of 1994. A sad but key pivot point in the evolution of all-truck, radio programmers and fans were increasingly turning toward this perky less-dour music."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: A Little Love and Some Tenderness Edition Part 1
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Biggest Band in America (1994)
facts.body: Going into 1994, Nirvana, alongside Pearl Jam, was regarded as one of the "unquestioned biggest bands in America," reflecting their immense influence and popularity. "Going into 1994, Nirvana and Pearl Jam were the unquestioned biggest bands in America."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: First Documented Public Fight (March 29, 1994)
facts.body: The initial recorded public altercation between Noel and Liam occurred at the Joiners Arms club in Southampton on March 29, 1994, where Noel punched Liam in the face and then chased him off stage during a show. "The first documented evidence of a public war between Noel and Liam was at a show at a club called Joiners Arms in Southampton on March 29, 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: NME Interview Incident (April 1994)
facts.body: About a month after their Southampton fight, Noel and Liam were featured in their first major British music media interview by the NME, conducted by John Harris at a Glasgow hotel in April 1994. The interview quickly descended into a profanity-laced argument between the brothers within the first three minutes, highlighting their intense relationship early in their career. "The interview took place at a hotel in Glasgow, the writer, a guy with the name of John Harris, reported it and it went something like this."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: NME Interview Single (1994)
facts.body: The chaotic NME interview, filled with the Gallagher brothers' arguments, was later released as a single, demonstrating the public's fascination with their relationship by reaching number 52 on the British charts. "That interview was later released as a single, and it reached number 52 on the British charts."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: First North American Tour (Fall 1994)
facts.body: Oasis embarked on their inaugural North American tour in the fall of 1994, a period marked by escalating conflict and drug use within the band. "In the fall of 1994, Oasis headed out on their first North American tour."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Whisky a Go Go Performance and Aftermath (September 29, 1994)
facts.body: During a performance at the Whisky a Go Go on Sunset Strip on September 29, 1994, Noel's insistence on singing harmonies alongside Liam's lead vocals agitated Liam. They repeatedly confronted each other on stage, culminating in Liam hitting Noel with a tambourine, leaving the stage, and refusing an encore. A backstage fight involving a thrown chair ensued, with Liam seen "skulking down Sunset Boulevard" and Noel departing with $8,000 of band money for Las Vegas and San Francisco, leading to the cancellation of more than half a dozen shows. "On September 29th, 1994, they played the whiskey a go-go on the sunset strip. Noel insisted on singing harmonies to lead lead vocals, which really annoyed Liam. They squared off on stage a bunch of times, and at the end of the set, Liam whacked Noel in the back of the head with a tambourine."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Near Breakup in 1994
facts.body: Following the chaotic Whisky a Go Go incident and Noel's temporary departure, the band was on the verge of breaking up, necessitating Noel's eventual return in Austin, Texas. "The band came this close to breaking up then."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Joiners Arms Incident – Noel Punches Liam (March 29, 1994)
facts.body: The first publicly documented physical altercation between Noel and Liam occurred at a show at the Joiners Arms club in Southampton. For an undisclosed reason, Noel punched Liam in the face and then chased him off stage. "The first documented evidence of a public war between Noel and Liam was at a show at a club called Joiners Arms in Southampton on March 29, 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: NME Interview – First Major Media Feature (April 1994)
facts.body: Approximately a month after the Joiners Arms incident, Noel and Liam were interviewed by the NME at a Glasgow hotel, their first major feature in the British music media. The interview, recorded by John Harris, quickly devolved into a heated argument, showcasing their volatile relationship. "This was their first major feature in the British music media."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: NME Interview Released as a Single (1994)
facts.body: The chaotic NME interview between Noel and Liam, which occurred in a Glasgow hotel, was later released as a single. This single reached number 52 on the British charts, demonstrating the early fascination the UK public had with the brothers' contentious relationship. "That interview was later released as a single and it reached number 52 on the British charts, which just goes to show you how much the UK was fascinated by this relationship this early in the band's career."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: First North American Tour – Offensive Lyrics and Whisky a Go-Go Fight (Fall 1994)
facts.body: During Oasis's first North American tour, Liam began changing song lyrics to be offensive, greatly annoying Noel, as they were his compositions. This culminated on September 29, 1994, at the Whisky a Go-Go in Los Angeles, where Noel's insistence on singing harmonies annoyed Liam, leading to multiple on-stage confrontations and Liam hitting Noel with a tambourine, refusing to return for the encore. "Liam started by changing the words of some of the songs into something rather offensive. This greatly annoyed noelle because of course they were his songs."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Whisky a Go-Go Aftermath – Noel Leaves Tour (September 29, 1994)
facts.body: Following the fight at the Whisky a Go-Go, Noel flew to Las Vegas and then San Francisco with $8,000 of the band's money to cool off, resulting in the cancellation of over half a dozen shows. He only rejoined the band in Austin, Texas, after which the band nearly broke up. It was later revealed that the entire band, including both brothers, was using crystal meth at the time. "Noelle, while he headed to the airport with $8,000 of the band's money."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Crystal Meth Use on First North American Tour (1994)
facts.body: During their first North American tour, the entire band, including Noel and Liam Gallagher, was heavily using crystal meth. This drug use contributed to the intense conflicts and instability that led to Noel temporarily leaving the tour after the Whisky a Go-Go incident. "What wasn't mentioned at the time was how the whole band, including Liam and Noelle, were off their nuts on crystal meth."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Dominant British Bands (End of 1994)
facts.body: By the end of 1994, Oasis was one of three bands dominating the British music scene, alongside Blur and Suede, indicating an impending explosion in the Britpop movement. "As we got to the end of 1994, three bands dominated the British music scene. There was Oasis, there was Blur, and there was Swade."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Intense Commercial and Label Pressure (1994-1995)
facts.body: From the release of their first single in April 1994, Oasis was subjected to a relentless schedule of concerts, single launches, album releases, and extensive tours. This intense commercial and label pressure, combined with the band members' youth, frequently led to public controversies, erratic behaviors, and outspoken interviews, with some statements later prompting apologies from the band. "son una presión comercial o rible, una presión discográfica horrible."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Fan Hearing Loss Lawsuit (1994) – Judge Awarded $34,000 Because No Warning Signs Were Posted
facts.body: On July 14, 1994, a French fan named Mohammed Falfana attended a U2 Zoo TV show at Stade Vélodrome in Marseille, one of 55,000 people present. Four years later, in September 1997, he filed suit claiming he had lost 75% of his hearing in his left ear and 49% in his right after security guards dragged him into a restricted area next to a speaker tower. U2's position was that he had entered the restricted area on his own initiative and so bore personal responsibility. However, the promoter had failed to post any warning signs advising that standing close to a 100,000-watt speaker system could damage hearing. The judge ruled on this technicality in Falfana's favor and awarded the equivalent of $34,000. "Nice technicality."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Reality Bites Soundtrack Contribution (1994)
facts.body: U2 contributed to the soundtrack for *Reality Bites*, a key film in the "slacker culture" movement released in 1994. The soundtrack also featured other notable artists like The Knack and Lisa Loeb. "The NAC, you two, and the Massive Hit for Lisa Loeb stay, I missed you."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.body: Although still popular in 1994, grunge appeared to be declining, with alt-rock fans beginning to seek out new sounds. "Grunge, although still very big in 1994, seemed to be on the wane."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Context in 1994
facts.body: For a young grunge fan in 1994, the historical context of Woodstock was as remote and unfamiliar as grunge might be to someone born after Kurt Cobain's death today. "Kurt, Grunge, and everything that happened in the early 1990s is as remote and unfamiliar to you as Woodstock was to a young Grunge fan in 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Fatigue and Decline by 1994
facts.body: By early 1994, the original Grunge movement was experiencing fatigue, with an proliferation of derivative "Grunge-like" and "Grunge-Lite" bands, while many of the authentic Grunge bands began losing momentum. This decline was exacerbated by public weariness with Kurt Cobain's complaints and personal drama, and the underwhelming sales of Nirvana's *In Utero*. "By the beginning of 1994, the original Grunge thing was looking very close to being beaten to death. The number of derivative bands really began to multiply. Too many Grunge-like bands and Grunge-Lite bands as many of the actual Grunge bands were starting to lose momentum."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Decline After Kurt Cobain's Death - April 1994
facts.body: Following Kurt Cobain's death in April 1994, grunge and the entire American alt-rock scene rapidly became "yesterday's news," entering a long, slow decline. This created a void that Britpop was well-positioned to fill. "When Kurt Cobain died in April 1994, Grunge in the entire American alt-roxene was suddenly yesterday's news and started a long, slow decline."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Anthony Kiedis's Rehab and Relapses (1994-1997)
facts.body: Kiedis's first serious rehab stint led to five years of sobriety, but he relapsed in January 1994 after a wisdom tooth extraction led to prescription narcotics (Vicodin and Percodan) and a return to cocaine and heroin. This cycle of getting straight and relapsing continued until 1997, including a stay at Exodus Recovery Center in Marina Del Rey, California. "His first serious trip to rehab left him sober for five years, but then there was a relapse in January 1994 when he had a wisdom tooth removed and the dentist put him on narcotics for the pain, which was a really bad idea."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

facts.title: Fighter Jet Crash near Alan Wilder (September 1, 1994)
facts.body: On September 1, 1994, while former keyboardist Alan Wilder was driving in the Scottish countryside, a Royal Air Force Tornado fighter jet on a training mission crashed less than 200 yards from his car. Wilder was covered in debris, and the two pilots were killed instantly, an event that profoundly affected his outlook on life. "It was September 1, 1994. Former keyboardist Alan Wilder was driving through the Scottish countryside when on a nowhere, a royal Air Force tornado, a fighter jet on a training mission roared over his car and crashed, less than 200 yards away."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Dave Gahan's Stage Fall (July 1994)
facts.body: In July 1994, Dave Gahan fell 12 feet off the stage in Indianapolis, resulting in multiple broken ribs. "We might as well include the time in July of 1994 when he fell 12 feet off the stage in Indianapolis and broke a bunch of ribs."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's Death Impact (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: While in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994, Depeche Mode learned of Kurt Cobain's death. Dave Gahan was reportedly taken aback by the news for a day or two before reverting to his usual drug-fueled habits. "De Peshmoan was in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994 when they heard about the death of Kurt Cobain."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Post-Devotional Tour Dispersal (1994)
facts.body: After the Devotional Tour concluded, the band members scattered, disinclined to see each other due to the severe strains and personal struggles experienced during the tour. "After the tour, everyone scattered. No one wanted to see each other."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Recording Second Album Pressure (1994)
facts.body: Under significant pressure from their record label, Radiohead was expected to complete their second album, "The Bends," by the summer of 1994. Consequently, they pre-booked a world tour. However, when the album remained unfinished by summer, the band was forced to interrupt their recording sessions "in midstream" to fulfill their concert commitments. This situation caused considerable anxiety among record companies on both sides of the Atlantic, who were eager for "another monster like Creep." "Everyone thought that the album would be finished by the summer of 1994, so they, under pressure from the record company, went ahead and booked a world tour."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Sierra Tucson Rehab and Relapse (1994-1996)
facts.body: Gahan underwent a period in the expensive Sierra Tucson rehab center in Arizona, which also attempted to help Ringo Starr, Whitney Houston, and Tiger Woods. Upon returning to Los Angeles, he found his house ransacked. He then overdosed on heroin, checking into the Sunset Marquis Hotel where he attempted suicide by slashing his wrists. After waking in a psych ward, he still only desired to get high and tried to hang himself in the bathroom. "There was a stint in rehab, the very expensive Sierra Tucson and Arizona."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Claimed First Musical Netcast (November 18, 1994)
facts.body: The Rolling Stones claimed to be the first band in cyberspace when they streamed about 20 minutes of their concert performance from the Cotton Bowl in Dallas onto the internet on November 18, 1994. However, this claim is disputed by evidence of earlier netcasts by other groups. "On November 18th, 1994, they dumped about 20 minutes of a performance of their concert at the Cotton Bowl and Dallas onto the internet."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts
