facts.title: Rejected Lollapalooza 1994 Headline Offer
facts.body: Kurt Cobain declined an offer of $10 million to headline the 1994 Lollapalooza Festival. "And then there was the $10 million that Kurt turned down to headline the 1994 Lala Pollusive Festival."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Death as a Career Move ｜ From the Archives
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Body Discovery Description (1994)
facts.body: A dramatic audio clip describing the scene of Kurt Cobain's death reports finding him with "a shotgun laying on his chest and the mud running out of his ear," an image that would later be confirmed by official reports of his suicide. "And then the kids through the last door, and they were just gay, and they were with the shotgun, and they left his chest, and the mud running out of his ear."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Discovery of Body (1994)
facts.body: On Friday, April 8th, 1994, an electrician discovered Kurt Cobain's body in a room above a greenhouse at his home. The electrician found him "laying there with a shotgun laying on his chest and blood running out of his ear," with the shotgun pointing at his neck. A suicide note was found stuck in a plant that had been dumped out. "The story began to unfold when any electrician noticed a body lying on the floor of a room above a greenhouse."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Official Death Confirmation (1994)
facts.body: On April 8th, 1994, at 4 p.m., Oscar Venet of the Seattle Police Media update information line announced that the King County Medical Examiner's office had positively identified Kurt Cobain's body by fingerprints. The autopsy confirmed he died of a shotgun wound to the head, which at the time appeared to be self-inflicted. The Seattle Police Department Homicide and King County Medical Examiner's offices continued their investigation. "The King County Medical Examiner's office has positively identified the body of Kurt Colbein by fingerprints."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide Note Excerpt (1994)
facts.body: An excerpt from Kurt Cobain's suicide note includes lines about his inability to fool people or himself, his concern about putting people off by faking it, his dramatic duty, and a wish for people to remember that "it's better to burn out than to fade away." The note concludes with "Peace, love, empathy, Kurt Colbein." "It's better to put it out. They just fade away. Peace, love, empathy, Kurt Colbein."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Impact of Suicide (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's suicide on April 8th, 1994, was described as the "seminal unifying and unforgettable moment for the new rock nation." For those "around then and into music," the day was said to be unforgettable. "If you are around then and into music, you will never, ever, ever, ever, forget that day."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Attempted Suicide in Rome (March 3, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain was found unconscious on the floor of room 541 at the Excelsior Hotel in Rome on March 3, 1994, after consuming up to 50 Rohypnol pills in addition to alcohol. He had been suffering from extreme depression, calling Courtney Love numerous times expressing hatred for "everything and everybody" after a series of European tour shows were canceled due to a throat issue. Courtney Love flew to Rome to meet him; they ordered room service and champagne before going to bed. He was transported to Umberto Polyclinic Hospital for his stomach to be pumped, and later to Rome American Hospital where he regained consciousness. He left a suicide note that, according to Courtney, read in part, "My doctor says I would have to choose between life and death. I'm choosing death." This incident was widely seen as an attempted suicide, predating his actual death by just over a month. "Nirvana and Kurt Cobain, who very nearly died in room 541 of the Excelsior Hotel in Rome on March 3, 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death and Rehab Attempt (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's death was reported on April 8, 1994, affecting Dave Gahan during Depeche Mode's tour in Buenos Aires. Cobain had also attempted to get clean at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, a week before his death. "De Peshmoan was in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994 when they heard about the death of Kurt Cobain."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Last Nirvana Show (Munich, March 1994)
facts.body: Nirvana's final concert took place in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, in March 1994, in front of just over 3,000 people. The gig was described as "okay," featuring a power failure that led to a quick acoustic set, despite Kurt feeling very sick with a sore throat. "Nirvana's last ever show was held in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany. In March of 1994, in front of just over 3,000 people."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Rome Overdose (March 4, 1994)
facts.body: While in Rome, Kurt checked into room 541 of the Excelsior Hotel with Courtney Love. Sometime after midnight on March 4, he wrote a three-page suicide note, ingested over 50 Rohypnol pills with champagne, and slipped into a coma. Courtney found him and called an ambulance, and he remained in a coma for 20 hours, with CNN even reporting his death. "Sometime after midnight on March 4, Kurt wrote a three-page suicide note, washed down more than 50 pills of a tranquilizer called Rohipno with a bottle of champagne and slipped into a coma."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: March 18, 1994 Domestic Dispute
facts.body: Following his return home to Seattle on March 12, another domestic dispute occurred on March 18, a Friday night. Kurt locked himself in a room and threatened to kill himself, prompting Courtney to call the police, who confiscated four guns and 25 boxes of assorted bullets. "On March 18, there was another domestic dispute of some kind. At Friday night, Kurt locked himself in a room and was threatened to kill himself, so Courtney called the cops again."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Last-Ditch Intervention (March 25, 1994)
facts.body: On March 25, Courtney organized an intervention at their Seattle home with doctors and friends, including Chris Novoselic, Dave Grohl, Pat Smear, Nirvana's management and legal team, and drug counselor James Burr. The meeting lasted five hours, and Kurt eventually agreed to enter rehab. "On March 25, Courtney gathered a bunch of doctors and friends together at the house in Seattle to try to scare Kurt straight. He had to deal with his problems."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Gun Purchase Through Dylan (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: Before flying to Los Angeles for rehab, Kurt and his friend Dylan visited Standbaker Sports, a Seattle gun shop, on March 30. Unable to buy a new gun himself due to police knowledge of his previous confiscations, Kurt gave Dylan $308.37 to purchase a Remington C-11 shotgun and a box of shells, claiming he needed it for protection. "So he gave Dylan the $308.37 to buy a Remington C-11 shotgun in the box of shells."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Exodus Recovery Center Escape (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles on March 30, but after two nights, on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, he scaled a garden wall, took a cab to the airport, and caught Delta flight 788 back to Seattle. "But on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, he scaled the wall in the garden, took a cab to the airport where he caught Delta flight 788 to Seattle."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On Delta flight 788 to Seattle, Kurt sat in seat 2F, next to Duff McKagan of Guns N' Roses. Upon landing, Duff offered him a ride home, which Kurt declined. "He ended up in seat 2F, next to Duff McCagan of Guns & Roses."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Last Autograph (April 2, 1994)
facts.body: Around 1 AM on Saturday, April 2nd, 1994, at Sea-Tac Airport, Kurt was recognized by a Canadian Nirvana fan who asked him to sign a copy of Jane Austen's "Mansfield Park." The autograph was strangely dated April 5th, the day Kurt ultimately died. "The weird thing about this autograph is that Kurt dated it as April 5th, which is the day he ended up killing himself."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Missing Persons Report & Detective Search (April 1994)
facts.body: Courtney Love, frantic and fearing Kurt would harm himself, hired an LA detective named Tom Grant to track him down. Kurt's mother also filed a missing persons report with the Seattle police. "She hired an LA detective named Tom Grant to track him down. His mother filed a missing persons report with the Seattle police."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Last Known Sighting and Activities (April 2-5, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt made it back to his Seattle home shortly before 2 AM on Saturday, April 2nd. One of the last people to see him alive was Callie, his former nanny, at about 6 AM that morning. He then attempted to call Courtney in Los Angeles but couldn't get through due to a "do not disturb" order on her phone. Over the next two days, there were "Elvis-like sightings" of Kurt around Seattle, including at a park, another house he owned in Carnation, with an unidentified friend at a dealer's house, at a couple of hotels, and reportedly at a store called CL Guns where he bought another box of 20 gauge shotgun shells. "One of the last persons to see him alive was Callie, the co-vain's former nanny who was looking after the house while everybody was supposed to be a Los Angeles."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide and Discovery (April 5-8, 1994)
facts.body: Sometime on April 5th, 1994, Kurt went to a room above the greenhouse in his backyard, wrote a suicide note, loaded a shotgun, injected himself with heroin, and shot himself. His body was found three days later on Friday, April 8th, 1994, by an electrician who saw him through a window. "One time on April 5th, 1994, he went to the room above the greenhouse in the backyard of his house. He wrote out a suicide note, loaded up a shotgun, loaded himself up with heroin, and shot himself."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Kindred Spirit Comparison (1994)
facts.body: Sinead O'Connor was believed by some to be a kindred spirit with Kurt Cobain, particularly around the time of her *Universal Mother* album's release in 1994. "And I somehow believe that she and Kurt Cobain were kindred spirits."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Exodus Recovery Center Stay (Spring 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain was a 27-year-old from Seattle who was at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey during spring 1994, at the same time Scott Wyland was considering checking into the facility for detox. "The second was a 27 year old guy from Seattle named Kurt Cobain."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Rehab Escape and Death (Spring 1994)
facts.body: Just a few days after Scott Wyland considered checking into rehab, Kurt Cobain escaped from the facility, made his way home, and subsequently died by suicide. This event significantly impacted Scott Wyland, exacerbating his own struggles. "And few days Kurt would escape from rehab, make his way home, and then shoot himself. This did not help Scott with his issues."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain died by suicide, found on Friday, April 8, 1994, in his Seattle home with a shotgun wound to the head and a suicide note nearby. He was 28 years old. "Kurt Cobain is in the news again. A body has been found in his Seattle home...Police in Seattle say the body of a man in his 20s has been found with a shotgun wound in the head at the home of Kurt Cobain of Nirvana."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Previous Drug Overdose (March 1994)
facts.body: The month before his death, Kurt Cobain was hospitalized in Rome for a drug overdose, specifically from painkillers and champagne. He was recuperating from this overdose prior to his death. "Last month, the late singer of Nirvana was hospitalized in Rome for a drug overdose...He had been recuperating from last month's overdose of painkillers and champagne."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994 is identified as occurring shortly after the peak of rock's fourth cycle, leading to the subsequent decline of alternative rock. "The peak for this cycle came shortly before Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death by Suicide (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain died in the early morning of Tuesday, April 5, 1994, by suicide via shotgun, preceded by a massive heroin overdose. His body was found approximately two weeks later, on April 8. His family and friends were aware he was in trouble, especially after a previous suicide attempt at a hotel in Rome. On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held at his Seattle home with his wife Courtney Love, bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team, lasting five hours. He seemed convinced to seek help and flew to LA on March 30 to check into the Exodus Recovery Center. However, he left on April 1 (Good Friday) by scaling a six-foot wall, flew back to Seattle, and disappeared. His final note, addressed to his imaginary friend "Boddah," was found in his pocket after he injected a large amount of Mexican black tar heroin and then used a Remington shotgun to kill himself in the greenhouse at his home. "He had injected so much heroin that he probably never even heard the gun go off."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Intervention Attempt (March 25, 1994)
facts.body: On March 25, 1994, Kurt Cobain's wife, Courtney Love, gathered a group of doctors and friends at their Seattle home for an intervention. The group included Courtney, Nirvana bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring Nirvana guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team. This intervention lasted for five hours and was an attempt to confront Kurt about his problems and convince him to seek help. "This intervention lasted for five hours. When it was all over, Kurt seemed convinced, and he flew to LA on the 30th to check into a rehab unit known for straightening out strong-out celebrities."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Rehab and Escape (March 30 - April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On March 30, 1994, Kurt Cobain flew to Los Angeles to check into the Exodus Recovery Center, a rehab unit known for helping celebrities. He spent two nights there. However, on the evening of Good Friday, April 1, he scaled a six-foot garden wall to escape, despite the terms of his stay allowing him to simply walk out the front door. He then took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. "He spent two nights, but on the evening of Good Friday able the first, he scaled the six-foot wall on the garden, which was kind of weird since the terms of his stay would have allowed him to just walk out the front door and check himself out."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Gun Purchase (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: Before going to Los Angeles for rehab, Kurt Cobain and his friend Dylan visited Stan Baker Sports, a Seattle gun shop, on March 30. Kurt wanted to buy a new gun because the police had confiscated his old ones, but he couldn't make the purchase himself as it would alert the authorities. Instead, he gave Dylan $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells, claiming he needed it for protection. "So he gave Dylan the $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells. Kurt claimed he needed for protection."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: While flying back to Seattle from Los Angeles on Delta Flight 788 after escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain coincidentally sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan in business class. McKagan reported that Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride to his house upon landing, but Kurt declined, signed an autograph, and then disappeared. "By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses' bass player, Duff McCagan. Duff says the Kurt seemed fine."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Final Activities and Suicide Note (Early April 5, 1994)
facts.body: In the early morning hours of Tuesday, April 5, Kurt Cobain woke up in his bed after sleeping in his clothes. He turned on MTV, found nothing interesting, then turned down the sound and put R.E.M.'s "Automatic for the People" album on his CD player. He lit three cigarettes while writing a note on a legal-sized notepad, addressed to his imaginary childhood friend, "Boddah." After finishing, he placed the note in his left coat pocket, retrieved a Remington shotgun, a box of shells, and a cigar box full of heroin from a hiding place. He also grabbed two towels from the linen closet, assuming someone might need them, and a can of Barks Root Beer from the fridge. He then went to a second-floor room in the greenhouse in his backyard, where he smoked five more cigarettes, added a few more lines to his note, and jammed the pen through the note into a pot of soil. He loaded three shells into the shotgun, cooked up $100 worth of Mexican black tar heroin into a syringe, injected it into his right arm, and before the full impact of the drug hit, he aimed and pulled the trigger. "The note was addressed to the imaginary friend he had known since he was a small child. It began to bata."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Intervention and Rome Suicide Attempt (1994)
facts.body: By the end of March 1994, Kurt Cobain's family, friends, and business associates were acutely aware of his troubles, especially after a previous suicide attempt at a hotel in Rome. On March 25th, 1994, his wife, Courtney Love, organized a five-hour intervention at their Seattle home with doctors, friends, bandmates (Chris Novoselic, Dave Grohl, Pat Smear), and members of Nirvana's management and legal team, in an attempt to compel him to address his problems. "He'd already attended suicide once at a hotel in Rome, and people were afraid he'd try it again."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Rehab Check-in and Escape (1994)
facts.body: Following the intervention, Kurt Cobain appeared convinced to seek help and flew to Los Angeles on March 30th to check into the Exodus Recovery Center, a rehab facility known for treating struggling celebrities. However, after spending only two nights there, he scaled a six-foot garden wall on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, to escape, despite the terms of his stay allowing him to simply walk out the front door. "Kurt went to LA and checked into the Exodus recovery center that night. He spent two nights. But on the evening of Good Friday, able the first, he scaled the six-foot wall on the garden, which was kind of weird since the terms of his stay would have allowed him to just walk out the front door and check himself out."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Gun Purchase via Proxy (1994)
facts.body: On March 30th, before flying to Los Angeles, Kurt Cobain and his "buddy Dylan" visited Stan Baker's Sports, a Seattle gun shop. Kurt wanted to buy a new gun because the police had confiscated his previous ones, but he couldn't make the purchase himself without the police knowing. He therefore gave Dylan $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells, claiming it was for protection. "But he couldn't make the purchase because, well, then the police would know. So he gave Dylan the $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Return to Seattle and Final Days (1994)
facts.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. Coincidentally, he sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan in business class, who later reported Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride, which Kurt declined. He signed an autograph and then disappeared. He made it back to his house before 2 AM on Saturday, April 2nd, and was last seen by the Cobains' former nanny, Callie, and her girlfriend around 6 AM that morning. "He took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses bass player Duff McKagan."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Last Known Activities (1994)
facts.body: After returning to Seattle, Kurt Cobain attempted to call his wife Courtney at her Los Angeles hotel but couldn't get through due to a "do not disturb" order. Over the next two days, there were "Elvis-like sightings" of him around Seattle, including at a park, another house he owned in Carnation (with an unidentified friend), a dealer's house, several hotels, a restaurant, and a store called Seattle Guns, where he purchased a box of 20 gauge shotgun shells. "Kurt then tried to call Courtney at her hotel in Los Angeles, but she had a do not disturb order on her phone and he couldn't get through."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide Details (1994)
facts.body: In the early morning of Tuesday, April 5th, Kurt Cobain woke up in his bed, having slept in his clothes. He turned on MTV, found nothing interesting, then muted it to play R.E.M.'s "Automatic for the People" album. He lit a cigarette and wrote a suicide note on a legal-sized notepad, addressed to "Boddah," an imaginary friend from childhood, which he then tucked into his coat pocket. He retrieved a Remington shotgun, shells, and a cigar box full of heroin from a secret hiding place, grabbed two towels from the linen closet, and a can of Barks Root Beer from the fridge. He went to the greenhouse in the backyard, added more lines to his note, loaded three shells into the shotgun, cooked and injected $100 worth of Mexican black tar heroin into his right arm, and, before the full impact of the drug, managed to aim and pull the trigger. He likely injected so much heroin that he did not hear the gun discharge. "It began to bata. Three cigarettes later, the note was done. He stuck it in the left pocket of the code he was wearing."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Last Concert Performance (March 1, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's final live performance took place on March 1, 1994, at Terminal 1, an old airplane hangar in Munich, Germany, attended by approximately 3,000 people. Despite suffering from bronchitis and a sore throat, and experiencing a power failure that necessitated a quick acoustic set, Nirvana completed the gig. This concert marked the end of his touring career, as the remainder of the European tour was subsequently cancelled due to his poor health. "No one knew it at the time, but this would be Kurt Cobain's last concert appearance."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Rome Overdose and Suicide Attempt (March 4, 1994)
facts.body: While in Rome with Courtney Love, Kurt Cobain checked into room 541 of the Excelsior Hotel under the pseudonym "Kurt Poupon." After visiting the Vatican and purchasing gifts for Courtney, he wrote a three-page suicide note on hotel stationery and ingested at least 50 Rohypnol tablets, a drug typically used for insomnia but also known as the "date rape drug." Courtney discovered him in a coma at 6:15 am, with blood coming from his nose, a water cache in one hand, and the suicide note in the other. He was revived 20 hours later. "Kurt slipped into a coma, but Courtney found him in time at 6.15am."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Intervention and Brief Rehab Stay (March 25-April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held for Kurt Cobain, involving Nirvana members Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl, guitarist Pat Smear, management and legal team members, doctors, and drug counselor James Burr. The five-hour meeting persuaded Kurt to enter rehab, and he communicated his intention to rest and recover via his AOL account. On March 30, he checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles but departed just two days later on April 1, scaling a guard wall despite having checked in voluntarily. "That meeting lasted five hours. Kurt was convinced to try rehab and arrangements were made."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Purchase of Shotgun for "Protection" (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: On the morning he was scheduled to leave for rehab, Kurt Cobain, accompanied by his friend Dylan Carlson, visited Stan Baker's Sports, a gun store. Kurt stated he needed a new gun for protection, citing the confiscation of his previous collection by police. Carlson purchased a Rowington C-11 shotgun and a box of shells for Kurt, costing $308.17, and the weapon was taken back to the house. "Kurt had said that he needed a new gun for protection since the cops had confiscated his collection."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: After escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain took a cab to LAX and boarded Delta Flight 788 to Seattle, where he was assigned seat 2F in business class. To his surprise, Duff McKagan, the bassist for Guns N' Roses, was sitting next to him. The two musicians chatted during the three-hour flight, with McKagan offering Kurt a ride upon their arrival in Seattle, which Kurt declined. "He was surprised to see Duff McAgan of Guns n' Roses sitting right next to him."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Signing of "Mansfield Park" with Incorrect Date (April 2, 1994)
facts.body: In the early hours of Saturday, April 2, 1994, shortly after landing in Seattle, Kurt Cobain was recognized by a Toronto fan at the airport. The fan, who was reading Jane Austen's "Mansfield Park," requested an autograph. Kurt signed the book as "Kurt D. Cobain" but, for unknown reasons, dated it April 5, which would later become the day of his death. "Kurt signed it, Kurt D. Cobain, and for some reason he dated it April 5."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: "Mystery Days" Leading to Death (April 3-5, 1994)
facts.body: The three days between April 3 and April 5, 1994, leading up to Kurt Cobain's death, are largely considered a mystery, despite ongoing search efforts by a private detective and a missing person's report. During this time, Kurt was reportedly seen by various individuals around Seattle, including a taxi driver and friends, at a house he owned in Carnation, Washington, at a drug dealer's residence, and at several hotels. He also allegedly purchased a box of 20 gauge shotgun shells from a store called Seattle Guns. "The next couple of days, April 3, 4th, and 5th, 1994, are something of a mystery."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death by Apparent Suicide (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: Sometime on Tuesday, April 5, 1994, Kurt Cobain went to the room above the greenhouse in the backyard of his home at 171 Lake Washington Boulevard East. There, he injected himself with a large dose of heroin, placed the Remington shotgun in his mouth, and pulled the trigger. His body was discovered three days later, on the morning of Friday, April 8, by electrician Gary Smith, alongside a suicide note. "He injected himself with a large dose of heroin, put the gun in his mouth, and pulled the trigger."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Ashes and Stolen Teddy Bear (Post-1994)
facts.body: Following his cremation, some of Kurt Cobain's ashes were scattered along the banks of the Wishkah River in his hometown of Aberdeen, Washington. Courtney Love retained a portion of the ashes for a shrine in her home and kept more inside a teddy bear, which she carried with her. However, this teddy bear was stolen in 2008 and has never been recovered. "More were kept inside a teddy bear that she took with her, but that bear was stolen in 2008 and never recovered."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Unreleased Autopsy Report (1994)
facts.body: In 1994, the full autopsy report for Kurt Cobain was never officially released to the public, citing Washington State's privacy laws. This lack of transparency fueled early suspicions and ongoing conspiracy theories regarding the circumstances of his death. "Well, back in 1994, the full report was never released because of Washington State's privacy laws."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Tom Grant's Murder Theory (December 1994-Present)
facts.body: Tom Grant, a former cop and county sheriff's detective who ran the Grant Company, was initially hired by Courtney Love on Easter Sunday, April 3, 1994, to locate Kurt Cobain. After Kurt's death, Grant became convinced it was a murder, not a suicide, and began collecting information on his own. He claims to this day that the case was improperly closed, presenting various "items of evidence" to support his theory. "The Kurt was murdered story, really began in December 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Courtney Love's Missing Person Report Allegation (April 4, 1994)
facts.body: Tom Grant claims that on April 4, 1994, Courtney Love filed a missing person's report for Kurt, impersonating his mother, Wendy Cobain. The report stated, "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal," a wording that Grant believes was intentionally crafted to frame Kurt's subsequent death as a suicide, guiding the police investigation towards that conclusion. "It was Courtney that called that report in. I believe one of the reasons she did that in my own personal opinion is so that she could word the report because the wording on that missing persons report turned out to be a pretty important thing in this investigation."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Divorce Intentions and Will Changes (January-March 1994)
facts.body: Leading up to his death, Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love were reportedly experiencing significant marital difficulties, with discussions of divorce and legal papers being drawn up. Kurt also reportedly contacted attorney Rosemary Campbell to inquire about removing Courtney from his will, while Courtney herself sought a "meanest, most vicious divorce lawyer" and asked about changing a prenuptial agreement. A nanny observed "way too much will talk" during this period. "Courtney had apparently engaged her lawyer, Rosemary Campbell, to find, and I quote, the meanest, most vicious divorce lawyer she could."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Canceled Credit Card and Suspicious Activity (April 1-8, 1994)
facts.body: On April 1, 1994, the day Kurt Cobain escaped rehab, Courtney Love allegedly canceled his Mastercard. Private detective Tom Grant stated that Courtney initially claimed "someone" was using the card, later clarifying it was Kurt and she wanted to track him. After Kurt's body was discovered, the Mastercard was reportedly missing. On April 4, there were multiple attempts to get cash advances ($5,000, $2,500, $1,500) over the phone, and on the morning of April 8, someone attempted to purchase $43.29 worth of flowers using the card. "On April 4th, the day before he died, someone tried to use the card."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide Note Handwriting Discrepancies (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: Doubts were raised about the authenticity of Kurt Cobain's suicide note, with Tom Grant suggesting that portions were written by someone else due to variations in handwriting, differing pen pressure, or even the use of different writing instruments or ink colors. Grant believed much of the note sounded like a statement of retirement rather than suicide, and two handwriting analysts allegedly concurred. Furthermore, the note lacked references to his daughter or mother and featured only a small, unsigned "Kurt." "Looking at the handwriting, Grant believed that portions of the note were written by someone else."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Missing Toxicology Report Clarification (1994, 2024)
facts.body: A short toxicology report from 1994 indicated that Kurt Cobain's blood contained diazepam and 1.52 mg of morphine per liter. Pathologist Dr. Sarah Wecht argued this amount would incapacitate even hardcore addicts, making it impossible for Kurt to aim and fire a shotgun. However, ambiguity exists regarding whether the 1.52 mg represented a "free morphine count" (immediate dose) or a "total morphine count" (cumulative build-up from long-term use). Opinions lean towards a total count, which would negate the argument that he was too high to act. A leaked 2024 report confirmed the presence of various opioids and benzodiazepines but offered no further clarification on this crucial distinction. "More likely though, is that the results of the toxicology report were misinterpreted."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Crime Scene Anomaly Allegations (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: Various claims were made about inconsistencies at the crime scene. Witnesses, including electrician Gary Smith, reported Kurt Cobain's hair looked "combed." Contrary to initial reports, he had not barricaded the room; a stool against the door was too short to prevent it from opening. Additionally, the forensics report stated "no legible prints" were found on the shotgun. These details, particularly the lack of clear fingerprints and the un-barricaded door, were cited by conspiracy theorists as evidence suggesting foul play. "Several witnesses, including Gary Smith, the nutrition, thought that Kurt's hair looked like it had been combed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Discovery of Body (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's body was discovered at approximately 8:40 AM on April 8, 1994, by an electrician named Gary Smith. Smith subsequently contacted a local radio station, believing he had obtained a major news scoop. "He stumbled on the scene at about 840 on the morning of April 8, 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Official Cause of Death (1994)
facts.body: On April 8, 1994, the King County Medical Examiner issued a statement describing the cause of death as "A shotgun wound to the head and at this time the wound appears to be self-inflicted." Within 24 hours, his death was officially ruled a suicide. "24 hours later Kurt's death was officially declared a suicide."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Divorce Intentions (1994)
facts.body: Prior to his death, there was evidence suggesting Kurt Cobain was attempting to divorce his wife, Courtney Love. This desire for divorce is considered by some investigators as a potential motive for foul play. "the evidence that Kurt was trying to divorce Courtney Love."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Sense of Danger (1994)
facts.body: During the final weeks of his life, Kurt Cobain reportedly believed that he was in some form of danger. This belief has been cited by conspiracy investigators as a point of suspicion surrounding his death. "Kurt believed that he was somehow in danger of, well, something during the last weeks of his life."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Disappearance from Rehab (1994)
facts.body: On April 1, 1994, Kurt Cobain disappeared from the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles after spending two nights in the facility. He subsequently flew back to Seattle the following morning. "On April 1, 1994, Kurt disappeared from the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Missing Credit Card (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's MasterCard was canceled by Courtney Love sometime on April 1, 1994. When his body was discovered, this credit card was missing. "When Kurt's body was discovered that card was missing."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Unusual Credit Card Activity (1994)
facts.body: Following the cancellation of his MasterCard, multiple attempts were made to use the card on April 4, 1994, and several subsequent days. These attempts included significant cash advances of $5,000, $2,500, and $1,500 over the phone. "one time the holder of the card tried to take a $5,000 cash advance over the phone."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Final Credit Card Attempt (1994)
facts.body: On the morning of April 8, 1994, the same day Kurt Cobain's body was found, an attempt was made to use his canceled credit card to purchase $43.29 worth of flowers. "somebody tried to use Kurt's credit card to buy $43.29 worth of flowers."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Missing Persons Report (1994)
facts.body: On Monday, April 4, 1994, a missing persons report for Kurt Cobain was filed. Courtney Love, his wife, made this call, pretending to be Kurt's mother, Wendy Cobain. "It was Courtney that called that report in."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Wording of Missing Persons Report (1994)
facts.body: The missing persons report filed for Kurt Cobain was worded as follows: "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal." This wording became a critical point in later investigations, particularly as it seemed to pre-emptively suggest the circumstances of his death. "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: House Search Omission (1994)
facts.body: On April 7, 1994, at 2:15 AM, Detective Tom Grant and Kurt Cobain's best friend, Dylan Carlson, conducted a thorough search of Cobain's house in Seattle. Despite searching "top to bottom," they failed to check the greenhouse in the backyard, as Carlson reportedly forgot to mention its existence to Grant. "They didn't go out into the backyard to check the greenhouse."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Presence of Diazepam and Morphine (1994)
facts.body: An autopsy on Kurt Cobain's body confirmed the presence of diazepam and a high concentration of 1.52 milligrams of morphine per liter of blood. Heroin, when injected, converts into morphine in the body, indicating a significant drug dose. "a concentration of 1.52 milligrams of morphine per liter of blood."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Incapacitating Drug Dose (1994)
facts.body: Dr. Cyril Wecht, a pathologist noted for his work on the JFK assassination, stated that such a high dose of morphine would incapacitate even hardcore addicts within seconds. He maintained that Kurt Cobain would have been unable to aim a gun and pull the trigger with that amount of drugs in his system. "Kurt would have never, ever been able to aim the gun and pull the trigger with that kind of smack in his bloodstream."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Questionable Method of Suicide (1994)
facts.body: Critics questioned why Kurt Cobain would use a shotgun to commit suicide, given the extremely high dose of heroin (morphine) in his system. It was suggested that a lethal injection of heroin would have allowed for a more peaceful death and a "better looking corpse." "Why not just inject a lethal dose of heroin, peacefully go to sleep, and die?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Combed Hair Appearance (1994)
facts.body: Several witnesses, including the electrician who discovered Kurt Cobain's body, reported that his hair appeared to have been combed. This observation was deemed unusual for someone who had just sustained a shotgun wound to the head. "it looked like Kurt's hair had been combed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Lack of Barricade (1994)
facts.body: Contrary to early reports, Kurt Cobain had not barricaded himself in the room above the greenhouse where his body was found. A stool was present by the door, but it was too short to effectively wedge the door shut. "Now there was a stool by the door, but it was too short to wedge the door shut."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Shotgun Load (1994)
facts.body: The shotgun found with Kurt Cobain contained three loaded shells. This raised questions for some investigators, who wondered why a person intending to kill themselves would load more than one shell. "If Kurt bought the gun to kill just himself, why would he load it up with more than one shell?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Disputed Fingerprint Evidence (1994)
facts.body: Police reports claimed that "Marks Fund" on Kurt Cobain's hands were consistent with firing a Remington M11 shotgun, but Detective Tom Grant stated he was unable to duplicate these results with his own M11. Furthermore, a forensics report from May 6, 1994, by senior ID technician T. Geronimo, stated that "The four cards of lifted latent prints contain no legible prints" from the shotgun. "The four cards of lifted latent prints contain no legible prints."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Greenhouse as Lookout (1994)
facts.body: Detective Tom Grant firmly believed that Kurt Cobain was using the greenhouse as a "little lookout tower" over his property and was in fear of his life. Grant hypothesized that Cobain intended to fly out of Seattle within hours or days, suggesting he was preparing to leave. "That was like a little lookout tower for him over his whole property. And I do firmly believe that he was in fear of his life."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide Note Analysis (1994)
facts.body: Detective Tom Grant did not believe the note found near Kurt Cobain's body was a suicide note, but rather a "retirement speech" to his fans. He noted that the last five lines, which included the phrase "which will be happier without me," appeared to be in a different handwriting, a conclusion supported by two handwriting analysts. "the last five lines of the note look like they were in someone else's handwriting."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Absence of Explicit Suicide Wish in Note (1994)
facts.body: The alleged suicide note found with Kurt Cobain's body contains no explicit statement from him about wanting to kill himself. This observation is a key point for those questioning the official suicide verdict. "no where the note does Kurt say anything about wanting to kill himself."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Second Note Discovery (1994)
facts.body: Courtney Love claimed that several months after Kurt Cobain's death, she discovered a second note from him in a sealed envelope under pillows in her bedroom. This discovery was considered odd because Tom Grant and Dylan Carlson had searched "everywhere including under pillows and mattresses" on April 7, 1994, without finding it. "This is rather odd because when Tom and Dylan searched the house on the morning of April the 7th, they looked everywhere including under pillows and mattresses, but Courtney insists that's where she found this letter."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Content of Second Note (1994)
facts.body: The second note, allegedly found by Courtney Love, was not suicidal in nature. Instead, it purportedly stated that Kurt Cobain was leaving her and Seattle. "Kurt allegedly tells Courtney that he's leaving her and Seattle."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Lack of Letters to Family (1994)
facts.body: A point of contention for investigators is why Kurt Cobain did not leave any letters or messages for his mother or his daughter, Frances Bean, if he intended to take his own life. "why didn't Kurt leave anything for his mum or his daughter?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Disputed Internet Photo (Post-1994)
facts.body: Detective Tom Grant asserts that an infamous internet photo circulating of Kurt Cobain's head after his death is a fake. He believes it is a "stock autopsy photo of someone who got caught in a lawnmower" and that the actual wounds, while fatal, were not as dramatic or severe as depicted. "He maintains it's just some stock autopsy photo of someone who got caught in a lawnmower."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Lack of Exit Wound (Post-1994)
facts.body: Lee Remington, an investigator from Seattle, elaborated on inconsistencies regarding the fatal head wound. He claimed that even with a light load in the shotgun, there should have been more damage and, critically, no exit wound. Remington concluded that it would have been impossible for someone to shoot themselves in the head in the manner Kurt Cobain was found. "he believes that it was impossible for someone to shoot themselves in the head the way Kurt Cobain was."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Unsigned Suicide Note (Post-1994)
facts.body: Lee Remington pointed out that the suicide note attributed to Kurt Cobain was not signed with a full signature; instead, the name "Kurt" was merely "printed out in small letters." "the suicide note wasn't signed. Kurt was printed out in small letters, no signature."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Financial Motive for Murder (Post-1994)
facts.body: Courtney Love's biological father, Hank Harrison, suggested a strong financial motive for Kurt Cobain's death. He posited that if Cobain had lived that weekend, he would have withdrawn all his money from bank funds, signed divorce papers, and other contracts, which would have significantly cut Courtney and other individuals out of substantial sums. "Kurt hadn't been chilled that weekend, he would have gone to the bank and taken all the money out of the funds."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Mother's Dismissal of Tom Grant (Post-1994)
facts.body: Wendy Cobain, Kurt's mother, issued a statement dismissing Detective Tom Grant as an "inept private investigator" and a "sleaze bag." She accused him of trying to gain "15 minutes of fame" and noted that the family had unsuccessfully tried for months to get him to sign a confidentiality agreement. "Tom Grant is the same inept private investigator who was hired by the family to find Kurt the week he was missing."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: "Mystery Days" Leading to Death (April 3-5, 1994)
facts.body: The three days between April 3 and April 5, 1994, leading up to Kurt Cobain's death, are largely considered a mystery, despite ongoing search efforts by a private detective and a missing person's report. During this time, Kurt was reportedly seen by various individuals around Seattle, including a taxi driver and friends, at a house he owned in Carnation, Washington, at a drug dealer's residence, and at several hotels. He also allegedly purchased a box of 20 gauge shotgun shells from a store called Seattle Guns. "The next couple of days, April 3, 4th, and 5th, 1994, are something of a mystery."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Absence of Explicit Suicide Wish in Note (1994)
facts.body: The alleged suicide note found with Kurt Cobain's body contains no explicit statement from him about wanting to kill himself. This observation is a key point for those questioning the official suicide verdict. "no where the note does Kurt say anything about wanting to kill himself."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Ashes and Stolen Teddy Bear (Post-1994)
facts.body: Following his cremation, some of Kurt Cobain's ashes were scattered along the banks of the Wishkah River in his hometown of Aberdeen, Washington. Courtney Love retained a portion of the ashes for a shrine in her home and kept more inside a teddy bear, which she carried with her. However, this teddy bear was stolen in 2008 and has never been recovered. "More were kept inside a teddy bear that she took with her, but that bear was stolen in 2008 and never recovered."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Attempted Suicide in Rome (March 3, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain was found unconscious on the floor of room 541 at the Excelsior Hotel in Rome on March 3, 1994, after consuming up to 50 Rohypnol pills in addition to alcohol. He had been suffering from extreme depression, calling Courtney Love numerous times expressing hatred for "everything and everybody" after a series of European tour shows were canceled due to a throat issue. Courtney Love flew to Rome to meet him; they ordered room service and champagne before going to bed. He was transported to Umberto Polyclinic Hospital for his stomach to be pumped, and later to Rome American Hospital where he regained consciousness. He left a suicide note that, according to Courtney, read in part, "My doctor says I would have to choose between life and death. I'm choosing death." This incident was widely seen as an attempted suicide, predating his actual death by just over a month. "Nirvana and Kurt Cobain, who very nearly died in room 541 of the Excelsior Hotel in Rome on March 3, 1994."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Discovery of Body (1994)
facts.body: A dramatic audio clip describing the scene of Kurt Cobain's death reports finding him with "a shotgun laying on his chest and the mud running out of his ear," an image that would later be confirmed by official reports of his suicide. "And then the kids through the last door, and they were just gay, and they were with the shotgun, and they left his chest, and the mud running out of his ear."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Canceled Credit Card and Suspicious Activity (April 1-8, 1994)
facts.body: On April 1, 1994, the day Kurt Cobain escaped rehab, Courtney Love allegedly canceled his Mastercard. Private detective Tom Grant stated that Courtney initially claimed "someone" was using the card, later clarifying it was Kurt and she wanted to track him. After Kurt's body was discovered, the Mastercard was reportedly missing. On April 4, there were multiple attempts to get cash advances ($5,000, $2,500, $1,500) over the phone, and on the morning of April 8, someone attempted to purchase $43.29 worth of flowers using the card. "On April 4th, the day before he died, someone tried to use the card."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Combed Hair Appearance (1994)
facts.body: Several witnesses, including the electrician who discovered Kurt Cobain's body, reported that his hair appeared to have been combed. This observation was deemed unusual for someone who had just sustained a shotgun wound to the head. "it looked like Kurt's hair had been combed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Second Note Discovery (1994)
facts.body: The second note, allegedly found by Courtney Love, was not suicidal in nature. Instead, it purportedly stated that Kurt Cobain was leaving her and Seattle. "Kurt allegedly tells Courtney that he's leaving her and Seattle."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Courtney Love's Missing Person Report Allegation (April 4, 1994)
facts.body: Tom Grant claims that on April 4, 1994, Courtney Love filed a missing person's report for Kurt, impersonating his mother, Wendy Cobain. The report stated, "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal," a wording that Grant believes was intentionally crafted to frame Kurt's subsequent death as a suicide, guiding the police investigation towards that conclusion. "It was Courtney that called that report in. I believe one of the reasons she did that in my own personal opinion is so that she could word the report because the wording on that missing persons report turned out to be a pretty important thing in this investigation."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Crime Scene Anomaly Allegations (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: Various claims were made about inconsistencies at the crime scene. Witnesses, including electrician Gary Smith, reported Kurt Cobain's hair looked "combed." Contrary to initial reports, he had not barricaded the room; a stool against the door was too short to prevent it from opening. Additionally, the forensics report stated "no legible prints" were found on the shotgun. These details, particularly the lack of clear fingerprints and the un-barricaded door, were cited by conspiracy theorists as evidence suggesting foul play. "Several witnesses, including Gary Smith, the nutrition, thought that Kurt's hair looked like it had been combed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death (April 8, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain died by suicide, found on Friday, April 8, 1994, in his Seattle home with a shotgun wound to the head and a suicide note nearby. He was 28 years old. "Kurt Cobain is in the news again. A body has been found in his Seattle home...Police in Seattle say the body of a man in his 20s has been found with a shotgun wound in the head at the home of Kurt Cobain of Nirvana."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death and Rehab Attempt (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's death was reported on April 8, 1994, affecting Dave Gahan during Depeche Mode's tour in Buenos Aires. Cobain had also attempted to get clean at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, a week before his death. "De Peshmoan was in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994 when they heard about the death of Kurt Cobain."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death by Suicide (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: Sometime on Tuesday, April 5, 1994, Kurt Cobain went to the room above the greenhouse in the backyard of his home at 171 Lake Washington Boulevard East. There, he injected himself with a large dose of heroin, placed the Remington shotgun in his mouth, and pulled the trigger. His body was discovered three days later, on the morning of Friday, April 8, by electrician Gary Smith, alongside a suicide note. "He injected himself with a large dose of heroin, put the gun in his mouth, and pulled the trigger."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Death by Suicide (April 5, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain died in the early morning of Tuesday, April 5, 1994, by suicide via shotgun, preceded by a massive heroin overdose. His body was found approximately two weeks later, on April 8. His family and friends were aware he was in trouble, especially after a previous suicide attempt at a hotel in Rome. On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held at his Seattle home with his wife Courtney Love, bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team, lasting five hours. He seemed convinced to seek help and flew to LA on March 30 to check into the Exodus Recovery Center. However, he left on April 1 (Good Friday) by scaling a six-foot wall, flew back to Seattle, and disappeared. His final note, addressed to his imaginary friend "Boddah," was found in his pocket after he injected a large amount of Mexican black tar heroin and then used a Remington shotgun to kill himself in the greenhouse at his home. "He had injected so much heroin that he probably never even heard the gun go off."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Disappearance from Rehab (1994)
facts.body: On April 1, 1994, Kurt Cobain disappeared from the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles after spending two nights in the facility. He subsequently flew back to Seattle the following morning. "On April 1, 1994, Kurt disappeared from the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Discovery of Body (1994)
facts.body: The body of Kurt Cobain was found by an electrician who was doing work at his Seattle home on April 8, 1994. The electrician saw the body through a window, leading police to break into a cottage above a detached garage where they found the body and a suicide note. "Police say the body was found this morning by an electrician who had been doing some work at the home. He saw the body through a window and police had to break into the cottage above a detached garage where they discovered the man and a suicide note."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Disputed Fingerprint Evidence (1994)
facts.body: Police reports claimed that "Marks Fund" on Kurt Cobain's hands were consistent with firing a Remington M11 shotgun, but Detective Tom Grant stated he was unable to duplicate these results with his own M11. Furthermore, a forensics report from May 6, 1994, by senior ID technician T. Geronimo, stated that "The four cards of lifted latent prints contain no legible prints" from the shotgun. "The four cards of lifted latent prints contain no legible prints."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Disputed Internet Photo (Post-1994)
facts.body: Detective Tom Grant asserts that an infamous internet photo circulating of Kurt Cobain's head after his death is a fake. He believes it is a "stock autopsy photo of someone who got caught in a lawnmower" and that the actual wounds, while fatal, were not as dramatic or severe as depicted. "He maintains it's just some stock autopsy photo of someone who got caught in a lawnmower."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Divorce Intentions (1994)
facts.body: Prior to his death, there was evidence suggesting Kurt Cobain was attempting to divorce his wife, Courtney Love. This desire for divorce is considered by some investigators as a potential motive for foul play. "the evidence that Kurt was trying to divorce Courtney Love."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Divorce Intentions and Will Changes (January-March 1994)
facts.body: Leading up to his death, Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love were reportedly experiencing significant marital difficulties, with discussions of divorce and legal papers being drawn up. Kurt also reportedly contacted attorney Rosemary Campbell to inquire about removing Courtney from his will, while Courtney herself sought a "meanest, most vicious divorce lawyer" and asked about changing a prenuptial agreement. A nanny observed "way too much will talk" during this period. "Courtney had apparently engaged her lawyer, Rosemary Campbell, to find, and I quote, the meanest, most vicious divorce lawyer she could."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Encounter with Duff McKagan (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: While flying back to Seattle from Los Angeles on Delta Flight 788 after escaping rehab, Kurt Cobain coincidentally sat next to Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan in business class. McKagan reported that Kurt seemed fine and even offered him a ride to his house upon landing, but Kurt declined, signed an autograph, and then disappeared. "By coincidence, sitting next to him in business class was Guns and Roses' bass player, Duff McCagan. Duff says the Kurt seemed fine."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Exodus Recovery Center Escape (April 1, 1994)
facts.body: Kurt checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles on March 30, but after two nights, on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, he scaled a garden wall, took a cab to the airport, and caught Delta flight 788 back to Seattle. "But on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, he scaled the wall in the garden, took a cab to the airport where he caught Delta flight 788 to Seattle."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Exodus Recovery Center Stay (Spring 1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain was a 27-year-old from Seattle who was at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey during spring 1994, at the same time Scott Wyland was considering checking into the facility for detox. "The second was a 27 year old guy from Seattle named Kurt Cobain."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Final Activities and Suicide Note (Early April 5, 1994)
facts.body: In the early morning hours of Tuesday, April 5, Kurt Cobain woke up in his bed after sleeping in his clothes. He turned on MTV, found nothing interesting, then turned down the sound and put R.E.M.'s "Automatic for the People" album on his CD player. He lit three cigarettes while writing a note on a legal-sized notepad, addressed to his imaginary childhood friend, "Boddah." After finishing, he placed the note in his left coat pocket, retrieved a Remington shotgun, a box of shells, and a cigar box full of heroin from a hiding place. He also grabbed two towels from the linen closet, assuming someone might need them, and a can of Barks Root Beer from the fridge. He then went to a second-floor room in the greenhouse in his backyard, where he smoked five more cigarettes, added a few more lines to his note, and jammed the pen through the note into a pot of soil. He loaded three shells into the shotgun, cooked up $100 worth of Mexican black tar heroin into a syringe, injected it into his right arm, and before the full impact of the drug hit, he aimed and pulled the trigger. "The note was addressed to the imaginary friend he had known since he was a small child. It began to bata."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Final Credit Card Attempt (1994)
facts.body: On the morning of April 8, 1994, the same day Kurt Cobain's body was found, an attempt was made to use his canceled credit card to purchase $43.29 worth of flowers. "somebody tried to use Kurt's credit card to buy $43.29 worth of flowers."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Financial Motive for Murder (Post-1994)
facts.body: Courtney Love's biological father, Hank Harrison, suggested a strong financial motive for Kurt Cobain's death. He posited that if Cobain had lived that weekend, he would have withdrawn all his money from bank funds, signed divorce papers, and other contracts, which would have significantly cut Courtney and other individuals out of substantial sums. "Kurt hadn't been chilled that weekend, he would have gone to the bank and taken all the money out of the funds."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Greenhouse as Lookout (1994)
facts.body: Detective Tom Grant firmly believed that Kurt Cobain was using the greenhouse as a "little lookout tower" over his property and was in fear of his life. Grant hypothesized that Cobain intended to fly out of Seattle within hours or days, suggesting he was preparing to leave. "That was like a little lookout tower for him over his whole property. And I do firmly believe that he was in fear of his life."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Gun Purchase Through Dylan (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: Before going to Los Angeles for rehab, Kurt Cobain and his friend Dylan visited Stan Baker Sports, a Seattle gun shop, on March 30. Kurt wanted to buy a new gun because the police had confiscated his old ones, but he couldn't make the purchase himself as it would alert the authorities. Instead, he gave Dylan $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells, claiming he needed it for protection. "So he gave Dylan the $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells. Kurt claimed he needed for protection."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Gun Purchase Through Dylan (March 30, 1994)
facts.body: Before flying to Los Angeles for rehab, Kurt and his friend Dylan visited Standbaker Sports, a Seattle gun shop, on March 30. Unable to buy a new gun himself due to police knowledge of his previous confiscations, Kurt gave Dylan $308.37 to purchase a Remington C-11 shotgun and a box of shells, claiming he needed it for protection. "So he gave Dylan the $308.37 to buy a Remington C-11 shotgun in the box of shells."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Gun Purchase via Proxy (1994)
facts.body: On March 30th, before flying to Los Angeles, Kurt Cobain and his "buddy Dylan" visited Stan Baker's Sports, a Seattle gun shop. Kurt wanted to buy a new gun because the police had confiscated his previous ones, but he couldn't make the purchase himself without the police knowing. He therefore gave Dylan $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells, claiming it was for protection. "But he couldn't make the purchase because, well, then the police would know. So he gave Dylan the $308.37 to buy a Remington 11 shotgun and a box of shells."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: House Search Omission (1994)
facts.body: On April 7, 1994, at 2:15 AM, Detective Tom Grant and Kurt Cobain's best friend, Dylan Carlson, conducted a thorough search of Cobain's house in Seattle. Despite searching "top to bottom," they failed to check the greenhouse in the backyard, as Carlson reportedly forgot to mention its existence to Grant. "They didn't go out into the backyard to check the greenhouse."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Suicide (1994)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain's suicide on April 8th, 1994, was described as the "seminal unifying and unforgettable moment for the new rock nation." For those "around then and into music," the day was said to be unforgettable. "If you are around then and into music, you will never, ever, ever, ever, forget that day."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 10
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Incapacitating Drug Dose (1994)
facts.body: Dr. Cyril Wecht, a pathologist noted for his work on the JFK assassination, stated that such a high dose of morphine would incapacitate even hardcore addicts within seconds. He maintained that Kurt Cobain would have been unable to aim a gun and pull the trigger with that amount of drugs in his system. "Kurt would have never, ever been able to aim the gun and pull the trigger with that kind of smack in his bloodstream."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Intervention Attempt (March 25, 1994)
facts.body: On March 25, 1994, Kurt Cobain's wife, Courtney Love, gathered a group of doctors and friends at their Seattle home for an intervention. The group included Courtney, Nirvana bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring Nirvana guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team. This intervention lasted for five hours and was an attempt to confront Kurt about his problems and convince him to seek help. "This intervention lasted for five hours. When it was all over, Kurt seemed convinced, and he flew to LA on the 30th to check into a rehab unit known for straightening out strong-out celebrities."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Intervention and Brief Rehab Stay (March 25-April 1, 1994)
facts.body: On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held for Kurt Cobain, involving Nirvana members Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl, guitarist Pat Smear, management and legal team members, doctors, and drug counselor James Burr. The five-hour meeting persuaded Kurt to enter rehab, and he communicated his intention to rest and recover via his AOL account. On March 30, he checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles but departed just two days later on April 1, scaling a guard wall despite having checked in voluntarily. "That meeting lasted five hours. Kurt was convinced to try rehab and arrangements were made."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain

facts.title: Intervention and Rome Suicide Attempt (1994)
facts.body: By the end of March 1994, Kurt Cobain's family, friends, and business associates were acutely aware of his troubles, especially after a previous suicide attempt at a hotel in Rome. On March 25th, 1994, his wife, Courtney Love, organized a five-hour intervention at their Seattle home with doctors, friends, bandmates (Chris Novoselic, Dave Grohl, Pat Smear), and members of Nirvana's management and legal team, in an attempt to compel him to address his problems. "He'd already attended suicide once at a hotel in Rome, and people were afraid he'd try it again."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Kurt Cobain
